question: Is the drop in Noor's exercise a concern for muscle and bone loss in flight?
headline: Noor's exercise duration and energy expenditure show an attention status due to a progressive decline.

observations.text: Exercise duration dropped from 60 min to 10 min between 2026-10-12 and 2026-10-25, with a mean of 37 min compared to a baseline of 52.5 min.
Active energy expenditure fell from 300 kcal to 50 kcal between 2026-10-12 and 2026-10-25, with a mean of 185 kcal compared to a baseline of 241.667 kcal.
Both metrics have an attention status across evaluation windows from 2026-10-12 to 2026-10-26, with data quality marked as degraded due to missing data.

evidence_context.text: Exercise programs are the main countermeasure protecting muscle and bone, though current exercise does not prevent substantial loss in calf muscles after six months.
Exercise training before flight improves performance on the station, and equipment has advanced from the rowing ergometer of Skylab to the motorised treadmill of the International Space Station.

uncertainties.text: 'attention' is produced by screening settings chosen for this demonstration. They are not clinical thresholds, and the screen is not a statistical significance test.
All crew data in this explanation is simulated. It shows how the software behaves, not how a person responds to spaceflight.
The cited summaries of published sources are general context about spaceflight. They do not describe this crew member and do not validate the screening settings.
No stored result explained here concerns muscle strength. Cited summaries on this subject are background only and cannot be applied to this crew member.
A second model (medgemma) reviewed the readings. Its verdicts are a model's opinion, not a validated clinical assessment.
The cause of the progressive reduction in exercise duration and energy expenditure remains unknown.
Second-opinion model (medgemma): The facts state the attention status indicates a trigger, not a physiological event.
Second-opinion model (medgemma): The facts state no physiological conclusion is possible regarding bone density or muscle strength.
